Bill.BriefDescription: Prohibiting specified sex offenses against children.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to sex offenses against minors; adding new sectionsto chapter 9A.44 RCW; and prescribing penalties.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 9A.44 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) A person is guilty of rape of a child in the fourth degree whenthe person has sexual intercourse with another who is at least sixteenyears old but less than eighteen years old and not married to theperpetrator and the perpetrator is at least sixty months older than thevictim. (2) Rape of a child in the fourth degree is a gross misdemeanor.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 9A.44 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) A person is guilty of child molestation in the fourth degreewhen the person has, or knowingly causes another person under the ageof eighteen to have, sexual contact with another who is at leastsixteen years old but less than eighteen years old and not married to p. 1 HB 3371the perpetrator and the perpetrator is at least sixty months older thanthe victim. (2) Child molestation in the fourth degree is a gross misdemeanor.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 9A.44 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: In a prosecution under section 1 or 2 of this act, it is anaffirmative defense that the defendant must prove by a preponderance ofthe evidence that the defendant did not know that the minor was sixteenor seventeen years of age.
